Forecast Discussion

Low pressure is over central North Carolina at midday, with a second, weaker low over the mountains. Rain tapers to showers this afternoon as both lift north.

An upper-level low moves from west Tennessee across Kentucky today and reaches Ohio by Friday morning, passing closer to us than it looked earlier this week. Colder air arrives tonight on its south side. Showers this evening change to snow showers from west to east.

Friday is cold and windy on a west wind. Snow showers and flurries fall mostly on the west side of the Appalachians. A lull is possible for a while Friday, but snow showers pick back up Friday evening and taper to flurries after midnight.

Snow accumulates mostly at higher elevations on the west side of the Appalachians. Marginal temperatures hinder accumulations below 3,800 feet, with a dusting mostly in the western two-thirds of the mountain region. The higher western elevations are another world.

High pressure builds over the Southeast Saturday. The day starts cold and gusty, then winds diminish and the afternoon moderates quickly.

Sunday, low pressure moves from Arkansas toward the Great Lakes, pulling a cold front toward us. Clouds return in the afternoon, and rain is possible late in the day, then falls Sunday evening. Colder air follows after midnight. Snow showers and flurries are possible by sunrise Monday, and flurries may linger Monday morning.

High pressure settles in Tuesday and Wednesday with dry, cool weather.
